result.summary:
INT-native-bridge-contract adversary against 30a4065036a917514fb4984fde73f87867f38619 (branch devin/1788854799-production-program-integration). Attack branch devin/pp/adv/native-bridge-contract-30a40650 @ 250434737ddd799e1730a466a556564aa66e597d adds ONLY two Jest files under apps/mobile/__tests__/adv/ (no production code, no existing test touched; `git diff --stat HEAD~1 HEAD` = 2 files, +1272). 35 attack tests in 14 groups. No P0/P1 found: every confirmed finding is P3 defense-in-depth on TS seams that either (a) belong to the session-capture surface which NO shipping screen invokes at this SHA (grep: only src/camera/capture.ts, src/flow/session.ts, src/flow/sessionNative.ts, src/data/offlineCapabilities.ts reference startSessionCapture/extractSessionEventClip/LiveSessionFlow), or (b) require a payload Swift does not emit.

COMMANDS/RESULTS (all VERIFIED, all run from apps/mobile after `npm ci` — the pre-existing node_modules lacked @sentry/react-native@8.24.0 and produced 20 unrelated tsc errors until reinstalled):
1. `npx tsc --noEmit` -> exit 0 (artifacts/adv/tsc.log, empty).
2. `npx jest --ci --silent __tests__/adv/nativeBridgeContract.session.attack.test.ts` -> exit 1; 19 executed, 13 passed, 6 failed, 0 skipped (artifacts/adv/session-attack.run2.log). Failing = breaks A1, A2, A3, A4(x2), A8-partial-bridge above.
3. `npx jest --ci --silent __tests__/adv/nativeBridgeContract.capture.attack.test.ts` -> exit 1; 16 executed, 15 passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped (artifacts/adv/capture-attack.run2.log). Failing = break B3-uri above.
4. Canonical full mobile suite `npx jest --ci --silent` -> exit 1; Test Suites 2 failed / 1 skipped / 313 passed (316); Tests 7 failed / 1 skipped / 6076 passed (6084) (artifacts/adv/mobile-jest-full.log). The 2 failing suites are exactly the two attack files (7 = 6+1); every pre-existing suite passes on HEAD, the skipped suite is pre-existing.

ATTACKS THAT DID NOT BREAK (passing tests are seam evidence; commands = #2 for A*, #3 for B*):
- A2 (numeric/missing sessionCaptureId receipt): rejected with 'invalid session receipt' and camera_startup_failed{invalid_session_receipt} recorded.
- A3 (native rejects stop with camera.session_not_found): error propagated verbatim with code.
- A4 control: a clip whose trigger mirrors the proposal is 'extracted'.
- A5 hostile motion payloads (string numerics, negative/infinite tMs, negative v, non-string captureId/emittedAtIso, missing fields, null/array/valueOf objects): all 13 dropped, droppedInvalidSamples()==13, engine never fed, valid sample after storm flows; unrelated event types and foreign captureId ignored without counting.
- A6 event ordering: late motion samples after flow.ended()/stop are ignored and the feed disconnects; out-of-order/replayed samples do not crash.
- A7 double start: second startSessionCapture while native reports camera.session_busy propagates the busy error unchanged.
- A8 permission denial / camera.session_start_failed / non-Error rejection: propagated verbatim with camera_startup_failed{native_session_start_error}; partial-bridge capability reporting itself (sessionCaptureAvailable()==false) is correct.
- A9 null-vs-omitted optional fields in extracted clip receipts: validator behaves identically for null and undefined where the contract says optional; required fields as null rejected.
- B1 permission denial then recovery: camera.permission_denied propagates verbatim, lock released, next capture and import start; synchronous native throw surfaces its own code (not camera.busy) and releases the lock.
- B2 settlement order after cancel: native rejecting with camera.interrupted after cancel still yields camera.cancelled; a poisoned native success (https uri) arriving after cancel is discarded, never validated/returned; a hung native op keeps the camera.busy barrier until native settles (documented recovery cost, not a break).
- B3 boundary: trigger.endMs === durationMs accepted, durationMs+1 rejected; evidence trackedDurationMs > trigger window rejected.
- B4 imported pose receipt: framesTotal == MAX_IMPORTED_POSE_FRAMES accepted, +1 rejected; sidecar frameCount drift / zero poses / framesWithPose>framesTotal rejected; seed {0,1} forwarded, seeds 1.0000001 / NaN / -0.0001 rejected before the bridge; all six camera.import_* failure codes survive runNativeCameraOperation and the lock is released.
- B5 byte-comparison echo: extra key, stale operationId, foreign receiptId, stringified expectedByteSize, status 'verified'/true, array echo -> all 'invalid'; default operation id matches Swift's ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$ and the request carries exactly {uri, operationId, byteSize, nativeMediaIdentity}; camera.byte_comparison_unavailable -> 'unavailable', camera.invalid_byte_comparison_request / undefined echo -> 'invalid'; account switch mid-comparison -> 'cancelled' even when native answers verified.

NOT_YET_VERIFIABLE (needs Xcode/simulator/device; NOT run per coordinator rule; exact command from a Mac checkout of 30a40650: `scripts/mac-full-verify.sh --remote`, or locally `scripts/mac-full-verify.sh`):
- INFERRED risk worth a native test: ClipMediaStore.exportStrokeWindow emits trigger.endMs = event.endMs - selectedStart (line ~1192) but durationMs = measured exported asset duration (line ~1337). When the rolling recording ends at/near the stroke end (selectedEnd clamped to artifact.lastFrameTimestampMs, e.g. stop immediately after a swing), frame-boundary rounding can make measured durationMs < trigger.endMs by a few ms and TS assertCapturedClip (isTrigger endMs <= durationMs) would reject the clip as 'invalid or incomplete'. Only an on-device export can confirm or refute.
- Swift-side mappings assumed by the TS tests: camera.session_busy on second start, camera.permission_denied, camera.session_not_found, camera.invalid_extraction_request, camera.extraction_failed, import_pose_extraction progress events carrying captureId/operationId, real compareCapturedClipBytes echo shape, and NativeEventEmitter delivery order under backgrounding.
- Simulator vs device: Vision body-pose availability, AVAssetExportSession passthrough behaviour and camera permission prompts.

Other observations (not breaks): assertCapturedClip accepts non-integer durationMs/postRollMs (Swift always emits Int); AnalyzeScreen import-progress matching accepts events with captureId === undefined after a run has latched an id (screen-level, not attacked here). No PR opened; nothing pushed to main or ci/mac-*; no force-push.
